name: RUBRIK, INC.
moat_justification: Gartner Leaders-box data-protection platform with security-led differentiation (immutable recovery, threat analytics, identity recovery) and subscription retention above 120% in company reporting — real lock-in once recovery workflows and protected estates sit on the platform, with subscription ARR $1.66B growing +33% YoY. Not 7-8: Veeam, Cohesity/Veritas, Commvault and Dell contest the same renewals, cloud-native entrants attack from below, there is no network effect, and pricing power is unproven through a cycle or in GAAP profits.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 8 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 48.8%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025, 2026 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
one_liner: Strong cyber-resilience franchise, moat 6/10, ARR +33% — but TTM SBC ($341.8M) exceeds all of its TTM operating cash flow ($337.1M), so owner's earnings are negative on every basis (TTM -$0.18/share) and it cannot clear the 15% hurdle at any price at $113.90; Tier F until SBC discipline shows up in a filing.
moat_for: Leader in backup and data protection with security-led differentiation — ransomware recovery, threat analytics, identity recovery
Subscription expansion in the base — ARR $1.66B (+33% YoY), $100k+ ARR customers +23% YoY, net retention above 120% in company reporting
Switching costs once recovery workflows, retention policies and protected estates are built on the platform
Asset-light, high gross-margin model with expansion paths into identity security and AI-agent governance
moat_against: Crowded Leaders box — Veeam, Cohesity/Veritas, Commvault and Dell contest the same enterprise renewals; no network effect
Cloud-native and hyperscaler-native protection tools attack the fastest-growing estates from below
Go-to-market runs through channel partners — distribution partly rented, partner concentration risk
Pricing power unproven through a full cycle as a public company (IPO 2024); no GAAP profitability yet
